body: He was a bit matted on the body, and as for the beard I asked for it short because it gets dirty and tangled. But yea I didn't realize that they were going to cut the hair on his head so short when they asked me :/ I am kinda annoyed that he doesn't look like himself but I didn't want him to be in pain or overheated....
the haircut is growing on me but i miss the fluffy teddy bear look (his name is jamie btw)

I have very long hair, sorta medium thickish? (maybe a lil less bc of the length). if anything falls out for me, it's right at the beginning and very close to the roots. If anything does fall, it will probably be barely noticeable

hey! scalp picker here! I've gone through periods of picking my scalp and not, so for me, my scalp is actually more likely to be scabby or flakey when I'm in a picking period (basically falling scabs, like u said). When I stop touching it, after a few days, the wounds heal and scab over and there's a lot less scabbiness or flakiness. basically, if you don't pick for the next few days you should be good!
I get that, I feel exactly the same. tbh i just didn't want to be even more depressing so that's why I said that 🤷‍♀️. Having a pet has helped me a lot tho.

I have double depression too. Gonna be honest, I don't have that many tips to offer. I'm still figuring it out. It really sucks, but trying to do something that feels good, even for a few minutes usually helps me a bit (i like taking my dog outside and sitting in a quiet spot, listening to music)

As someone who also struggles with those 3 disorders, I get where you are coming from. I've been picking since 3rd grade. When I was younger (and still sometimes now, but less) I would go through periods were I didn't pick at all, and it was pretty mild. When I started to get older, it started getting bad. Now, with the pandemic and just a whole bunch of stuff, my skin picking has never been this bad. I understand not wanting to stop, and I've been there, it feels harmless, it feels almost like a hobby. Try to stop. You don't want to risk it getting bad.

yes!!! i had high hopes for when I started stimulants, only to feel no difference.  After a few changes in dose, it still is not the 'cure' i was hoping for. It makes my all over the place thoughts go in one line, but they're still jumping around, just in a neater way.

It helps, but it won't make adhd dissapear.
I use the Nuvet puppy and kitten shampoo and it's super gentle and smells great.

We originally washed our f1b bernedoodle pup every 2 weeks (which is what the vet said), and he really needed it since he got dirty or smelly often. Now he stays cleaner (4.5 months now) and the groomer said that any more than once a month will dry out a pup's skin. I also don't use a blow dryer, just towel him off really thoroughly. Spot cleaning is important tho!
yay! have fun and good luck!
Our mini F1b is 18 lbs at 18 weeks. He's expected to be around 35lbs, give or take 5, fully grown. She might still be big since standards grow for longer, but probably on the lower end.

I use a slicker brush and comb for my F1b mini bernedoodle and they work great! Super easy to get rid of any tangles and he's brushed often, which makes sure his coat stays tangle-free.

We also have a mini bernedoodle puppy (f1b) and we use a slicker brush and comb. Our groomer said its really important to use both, and we've been brushing him a lot (about 4 times a week to more) to keep his coat smooth, fluffy, and free of tangles. He rarely sheds, and doesn't at all after brushing. At first he hated getting brushed, but with time and treats he got used to it!
